extracted.intended_audience: Members of the National Association of Science Writers, applicants/participants in NASW events/programs, and science writers more broadly
extracted.subtask_short: NASW code of ethics and conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational code of ethics and member conduct specifying ethical journalism standards, expected behaviors at NASW events (virtual and in-person), prohibited behaviors, reporting procedures, review processes, and possible consequences for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Science writers should strive to be accurate in their professional work, including verifying the accuracy of their information and checking sources’ credentials and their potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While anonymous sources may occasionally be necessary, these should be few and carefully considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination in reporting and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Science writers should refrain from discrimination based on race, color, national or ethnic origin, immigration status, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, age, disability, military service or veteran status, socioeconomic background or status, education, or belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrimination is not acceptable under any circumstances; NASW is committed to equality and to making science writing welcoming to all individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and plagiarism prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Science writers' work should be their own. Plagiarism is not acceptable under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present others' work or words as your own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to scientific controversy and consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Science writers should support the healthy exchange of views and opinions in science but also realize when scientific principles are no longer questioned by the majority of reputable scientists involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid giving undue weight to fringe views once consensus has been established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest avoidance and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Science writers should avoid any potential conflict of interest with an assignment, financial or otherwise. Conflicts that are unavoidable should be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose relationships, funding, or other interests that could influence coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Science writers should immediately admit published mistakes and make every effort to correct them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt acknowledgment and correction of errors to maintain accuracy and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to equality, diversity, equity, accessibility, inclusion (DEAI)
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW is committed to equality in opportunity and treatment and to diversity, equity, accessibility, and inclusion across all aspects of the organization and the broader field of science writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work to include perspectives of storytellers, subjects, and sources representing breadth of human experience; do not tolerate harassment, discrimination, or incivility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability of the code
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code of Ethics and Member Conduct applies to all NASW members (including elected officials, consultants, contractors and employees) and to all participants in NASW and NASW-sponsored events, virtual and in-person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership or participation constitutes agreement to adhere to the Code; acceptance of honors/awards or candidacy also constitutes agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: General expected behavior: respect and consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Members and participants SHALL treat all members, participants, attendees, staff, and vendors with respect and consideration, valuing a diversity of views and opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat others with dignity regardless of individual characteristics listed in the Values Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate thoughtfully and avoid personal attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate openly with respect for others, discussing and debating ideas rather than individuals. Members shall avoid personal attacks directed toward others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on ideas and evidence rather than ad hominem commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-awareness and non-dominance in discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate self-awareness and avoid dominating the discussion. Make space for members of historically marginalized groups when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of power differentials and make room for diverse voices in panels and group discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration and sensitivity to power differentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Be collaborative and mindful not to exert dominance over others; consider power differentials in relationships and communication modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for differences such as ease of communicating by video vs. audio; avoid behaviors that silence others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with venue/platform rules and event officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the rules and policies of the venue and/or platform. If a leader/facilitator or event official directs you to stop a behavior or delete a comment, comply immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After complying, questions or concerns may be raised with an event contact; directives are made to implement this policy or platform policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual meeting expectations: inclusion and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Welcome all forms of participation (video, audio, other). Help protect participants' personal privacy; display your name when logging on to virtual platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitators should invite discussion without pressuring; notify event contact if someone's camera exposes private information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online discussion/forum expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Gracefully accept well-communicated constructive criticism; refrain from doing online something you wouldn't do in another professional situation; sign written messages with your name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be civil, concise, and identify yourself in forum posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-person event expectations and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect venue rules and NASW Code; be mindful of surroundings and fellow participants; call emergency services or alert venue security if someone is in immediate danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendees found in violation may be asked to leave without refund and at their cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: harassment and abusive conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Harassment in any form — including sexual harassment, denigrating jokes, stereotyping, or a recurring pattern of disrespectful behavior — is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not engage in biased, demeaning, intimidating, coercive, or harassing/hostile conduct or commentary, whether seriously or in jest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: inappropriate favors and exploitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesting or accepting inappropriate favors from students, employees, or colleagues is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid abuse of positional power or relationships for personal gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: false or damaging claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempting to injure the reputation or professional opportunities of others by false, biased, or undocumented claims is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make factual, documented assertions; avoid defamatory or unfounded allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: verbal/written abuse and intimidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbal or written abuse or intimidation (in-person or remotely), including harmful comments related to protected characteristics, is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes comments in any medium that demean or threaten individuals or groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: photographing/recording/distribution without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographing, recording, or videotaping others and/or disseminating such media without their consent is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screenshots of slides/presenters are acceptable unless the presenter states otherwise; screenshots of attendees are not allowed without consent. Only NASW or its designees may record/distribute event media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: displaying graphic/explicit images without warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Displaying or distributing images or recordings involving bigotry, nudity, sexual images, gore, or violence in public spaces/presentations is prohibited unless relevant; an audience warning must be declared if such images are relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide content warnings and consider audience safety and context before showing graphic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: unwelcome physical behavior and threats
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentional, unwelcome physical behaviors (stalking, unwanted contact, aggressive displays) and threats of physical, emotional, professional, or financial harm are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes physical abuse, intimidation, stalking, and disregard for another's safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: violating boundaries and continuation of prohibited conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Violating communicated physical, emotional, or sexual boundaries through continued prohibited behaviors or comments is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect explicit and implicit boundaries of others; do not persist after being told to stop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: retaliatory or weaponized reporting behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Retaliatory behavior during or after the reporting process, or weaponizing the reporting process to further baseless allegations, is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to reporting parties, witnesses, and those reported; the reporting process should not be used to harm others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: creating or contributing to hostile environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any behavior that reasonably creates, contributes to, or maintains an environment hostile or unwelcoming toward a person or group is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes inciting, encouraging, or condoning prohibited behaviors and creating unsafe or exclusionary situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual-specific prohibitions: social media, appearance comments, disruption, recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: For virtual events: do not engage in prohibited behaviors on social media in ways associated with an NASW event; do not comment on personal appearance or reasons for participating by video/audio; do not disrupt events (e.g., 'zoom-bombing'); do not make or distribute recordings of the virtual event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only NASW or its designees may record/distribute event media. Screenshots of slides are OK unless presenter objects; screenshots of attendees require consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forum-specific prohibitions: off-topic, redundant, excessive, promotional posts
rubrics_metrics.description: In online discussion groups/forums, refrain from posting unrelated topics, redundant information, posting excessively, or writing excessively long posts; promotional materials or solicitations are prohibited unless expressly approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search archives before posting; adhere to forum-specific exceptions noted by moderators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member-specific restrictions on representing NASW
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless authorized by the NASW Board of Directors, members may not use NASW's name for personal fundraising, identify themselves as members in political writing/endorsements/fundraising or to promote a product/policy/company, or speak for the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must not imply NASW endorsement of political positions or personal activities without Board authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASW operating principle: political neutrality with exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW generally does not take political positions, endorse candidates, or allow use of its name in political events, but may take positions on issues related to journalism, freedom of information, and public policy that affect members' ability to practice journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such actions are determined by the Board of Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASW operating principle: fundraising and funding conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW may undertake fundraising and partnerships only with Board permission and may not accept funding from organizations or individuals whose aims conflict with NASW’s aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board or staff designees have authority to review and determine conflicts of interest related to funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to other policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of NASW whistleblower, antitrust, conflicts of interest, and honors/awards policies may also constitute violations of this Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full texts of these policies are available at nasw.org/otherpolicies and should be consulted for specifics (e.g., whistleblower protections, antitrust prohibitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting mechanism and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Any NASW member or participant can report harmful behavior or potential violations using NASW's reporting form; NASW will prioritize safety and confidentiality and can offer confidential reporting options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identity of reporting party will be kept confidential if they so wish until (and unless) disclosure is needed to address the problem and the reporter agrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fixed deadline for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no absolute deadline or statute of limitations for reporting potential violations to NASW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting parties are encouraged to come forward at any time so harm may be addressed and a safe environment maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely acknowledgment and investigation of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: A written report to NASW will be acknowledged and reviewed in a timely manner; NASW will ensure timely investigation of reported allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations may be conducted by the Board, Ethics Committee, Meeting Conduct Response Team, or a designated official, considering conflicts of interest and confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting Conduct Response Team (MCRT) composition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: For conference/event reports, the MCRT will consist of current NASW Board members and optionally trained volunteers who receive and process meeting conduct reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volunteers can include NASW members in good standing. MCRT handles meeting conduct reports, maintains confidentiality/anonymity as appropriate, and forwards decisions on consequences to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASW Ethics Committee role for non-event reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The NASW Ethics Committee will review member complaints/reports not associated with meetings or events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on consequences and enforcement remain the responsibility of the NASW Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of possible consequences and discretionary enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: NASW officials may take actions deemed necessary, including immediate removal from events, requiring an accused participant to leave event sites, disconnecting participants during virtual events, bans or suspensions from future participation, and other actions to protect inclusion and safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board or its designees may impose consequences before determining whether a violation occurred if a credible assertion requires immediate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal grounds and limited remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal of a decision is permitted only for new consequential facts, grossly disproportionate consequences compared to similar cases, lack of facts to support the decision, a conflict of interest by a decision-maker, or procedural failures with consequential effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only remedy for a successful appeal of a requirement to leave an event is a refund of the event's registration fee, if applicable.
